stemMd: Solid sodium chloride conducts electricity poorly, whereas molten sodium chloride conducts. Why?

options.label: A
options.textMd: Melting allows its ions to move through the material.

options.label: B
options.textMd: Molten salt conducts only because electrons form covalent bonds.

options.label: C
options.textMd: Melting converts all sodium chloride into copper.

explanationMd: Ions in the solid occupy lattice positions and cannot migrate freely. In the melt, mobile charged ions can carry current. The difference is mobility, not the initial absence of charge.

distractorRationale.b: Mobile ions carry charge in the melt.
distractorRationale.e: The lattice already contains ions, but they are fixed in place.
distractorRationale.c: A phase change does not change the substance into a metal.
distractorRationale.d: This is not a nuclear transformation.
